sourceEvidence.label: UniRouter PRD6 and X-Insight adaptive trust boundary evidence

assessment.summary: The evidence supports separating historical adaptive-risk analysis from locally owned, attenuation-only enforcement; the proposal is not implemented.

nonNegotiables: X-Insight is not a synchronous request, settlement, or failover dependency.
A risk assertion cannot grant authority absent from the subject's baseline entitlement.
Every irreversible side effect is mediated by the component that owns it.
Raw prompt and response persistence remains disabled by default.
No new cross-project runtime contract, deployment, paid shadow traffic, or continuous ingestion is authorized by this analysis.
assumptions: No production workload latency, memory, event-lag, revocation, or classifier-precision budget was supplied.
The accepted P6-F16 through P6-F21 prerequisites will be independently implemented and reviewed before adaptive enforcement.
Metadata-first fixtures are sufficient for the first design experiment.

opportunities.title: Split adaptive trust analysis from local enforcement
opportunities.summary: Keep cross-request analysis asynchronous while enforcing signed, expiring, attenuation-only decisions at UniRouter and each actual action owner.
opportunities.diagnosis: The current products separate live model dispatch from controlled evidence import, but future adaptive-risk ideas blur fact production, analysis, policy authority, and side-effect enforcement.

evidence.claim: UniRouter owns the live model authentication, admission, rate-limit, governance, and relay path but exposes no general Tool Gateway route.
Local policy seams exist, while the OpenAI-compatible streaming fallback can flush before semantic parsing.
The trusted evidence context is metadata intake, not an audience-bound, expiring, replay-resistant capability.
The accepted v1 cross-project contract is operator-mediated sidecar reconciliation.
Tenant, identity, financial terminal-state, stream, revocation, and fan-out risks must precede adaptive enforcement.
X-Insight Phase 1 lacks continuous ingestion, tenant/RBAC, trust scoring, policy publication, and evaluation orchestration.
The current X-Insight integration design keeps settlement, failover, and request success independent of X-Insight availability.
Historical risk analysis and irreversible-action enforcement require separate ownership because only the action owner can completely mediate the sink.

desiredInvariants: UniRouter never requires a synchronous X-Insight call for authentication, routing, settlement, stream termination, or response success.
Risk can attenuate but never elevate baseline authority.
Every irreversible action is checked by its provider, Tool Gateway, IAM, data, write, or export owner.
Observed facts, derived risk, compiled policy, and final enforcement decisions have distinct issuers and versions.
Invalid, cross-tenant, replayed, rolled-back, or expired assertions cannot become allow decisions.
Missing evidence is recorded as a gap and cannot be converted into a safe claim.

options.title: Gateway monolith
options.summary: Place adaptive analysis, historical state, policy decisions, and model enforcement inside UniRouter.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The gateway already owns model dispatch and can add local controls at existing seams.
Uniform pre-flush stream normalization remains required before any mandatory stream detector.
The option avoids a new online X-Insight dependency.
It avoids X-Insight gaps by duplicating future analysis inside UniRouter.

tradeoffs.assessment: Model-path checks become local, but analyzer compromise and resource exhaustion share a process with provider dispatch and billing; tool sinks still require separate mediation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run authorization-bypass, detector-compromise, and resource-exhaustion tests while verifying tool actions remain separately mediated.

tradeoffs.assessment: No network hop is added, but classifier inference, state queries, locks, and cache misses increase request tail latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare p50/p95/p99 latency and CPU for short Chat, long stream, Embeddings, and 100-child workloads with each detector enabled.

tradeoffs.assessment: The gateway must hold models, buffers, risk caches, graph or history state, and extra policy generations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure steady and peak RSS, allocations, retained policy generations, and stream-buffer growth under overload.

tradeoffs.assessment: Analysis faults and capacity contention share the gateway failure domain even though network dependency is avoided.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject detector stalls, panics, model load failure, state corruption, and CPU pressure while measuring model and settlement availability.

tradeoffs.assessment: One deployable remains, but it gains broader model, index, tuning, rollout, and incident responsibilities.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run policy/model upgrade and rollback drills and inventory the credentials and alerts required by the combined process.

tradeoffs.assessment: Deterministic local checks can be feature-flagged at existing seams, although mandatory historical state later makes rollback harder.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Enable one deterministic stage in shadow mode, roll it back across mixed versions, and verify the baseline remains complete.

residualRisks: Analyzer compromise or overload shares the gateway blast radius.
Historical state can become stale or corrupt inside the request service.
Tool, data, and export sinks remain outside UniRouter unless separately integrated.

workPackages: Complete identity, tenant, billing, capability, and stream prerequisites.
Add feature-flagged deterministic local policy stages before heavier analysis.
acceptanceCriteria: No mandatory detector can bypass baseline entitlement or leave a stream unaccounted.
Measured resource budgets remain within an explicitly accepted threshold.
migrationNotes: Keep the baseline policy complete so detector modules can be disabled safely.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the new detector generation and return to the prior reviewed local baseline through a reviewed change.

options.title: Synchronous central X-Insight decision service
options.summary: Query a central X-Insight policy decision service before each governed action.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The design requires a new contract that conflicts with the currently accepted sidecar-only boundary.
Authentication, tenant isolation, policy publication, analysis, and production operations do not currently exist.
The option contradicts the current no-request-dependency principle unless explicitly replaced.
It can centralize model decisions but cannot mediate tool sinks without additional integrations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Central state improves consistency, but central compromise or erroneous allow/deny decisions have a broad blast radius unless every sink rechecks baseline entitlement.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model analyzer and policy-service compromise, cross-tenant requests, bad broad policies, and local entitlement rechecks at every audience.

tradeoffs.assessment: Serialization, network, queueing, graph lookup, and detector work are added to each governed request.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark same-region and partitioned p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency with realistic decision payloads and detector load.

tradeoffs.assessment: Gateway memory can remain smaller, but the central service needs queues, graph indexes, models, caches, and per-tenant isolation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure central service RSS, queue depth, graph-index size, cache eviction, and per-tenant noisy-neighbor behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: A new central service and network partition become correlated request failure paths or create pressure for unsafe unlimited fail-open.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject timeout, partition, overload, region loss, retry storms, and stale responses while verifying policy-specific failure behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: A production tenant-aware authorization service needs regional capacity, SLA, authentication, rotation, incident response, and coordinated rollout.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete a production-readiness review and operate shadow traffic through deployment, key rotation, and disaster-recovery drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: The option changes the accepted availability contract and requires every action owner to adopt the remote protocol.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run unsigned and signed shadow comparison first, then prove mixed-version fallback and full rollback without losing local baseline enforcement.

residualRisks: Central outage or bad policy can affect many tenants and action owners.
Unsafe fail-open pressure remains during partitions or overload.
Tool and data systems still require their own complete mediation and local entitlement checks.

workPackages: Replace the accepted cross-project availability contract through an explicit decision.
Build and production-harden a tenant-aware authenticated policy decision service.
acceptanceCriteria: The central service meets an explicitly selected production SLA and every failure mode has a bounded policy outcome.
Every execution point rechecks baseline entitlement and rejects cross-tenant or replayed decisions.
migrationNotes: Keep local baseline policy complete throughout shadow and cutover.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the remote decision dependency and return all audiences to the prior reviewed local baseline.

options.title: Split plane with signed local enforcement
options.summary: Keep analysis asynchronous, compile attenuation-only policy, and enforce audience-specific snapshots at each actual action owner.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: UniRouter retains local authority for the model actions it owns, while other sinks remain first-class enforcement points.
The design needs the accepted normalized pre-flush stream hook before mandatory streaming policy.
P6-F19 capability and audience/expiry/epoch/replay semantics must replace any attempt to use evidence metadata as authority.
X-Insight remains off the request path and the current v1 contract stays unchanged until a separate async contract is accepted.
Tenant, identity, financial, revocation, and stream prerequisites remain mandatory tactical protections.
X-Insight can evolve its analysis separately, but ingestion, tenant/auth, policy publication, and evaluation capabilities still need their own acceptance.
The option preserves the no-request, settlement, and failover dependency invariant.
The proposed roles encode least privilege, complete mediation, dual-speed control, and explicit uncertainty.

tradeoffs.assessment: Facts, risk, policy, and enforcement are separated; the analyzer cannot grant authority and each irreversible sink retains complete mediation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prove privilege non-increase and run cross-tenant, wrong-audience, replay, epoch rollback, key compromise, and action-owner bypass tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local signature and cache checks add bounded work while deep analysis leaves the hot path, but no workload measurement exists yet.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare p50/p95/p99 added latency and CPU with local verification/cache enabled on short Chat, long stream, Embeddings, and 100-child loads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Execution points need bounded policy-generation and replay caches, while X-Insight needs analysis indexes and queues.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure and cap policy generations, replay IDs, stream buffers, queue depth, graph indexes, and peak RSS under update bursts.

tradeoffs.assessment: X-Insight and analysis outages do not add a request network dependency; unexpired local policy continues and expiry cannot increase privilege.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject analysis, publisher, network, cache, key-rotation, clock, and stale-state failures across multiple replicas.

tradeoffs.assessment: Separate issuers, schemas, keys, policy generations, conformance suites, and incident controls add operational work while narrowing failure domains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run signing-key rotation, generation rollback, broad-bad-risk containment, manual override, and cross-component incident drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: Observe, signed shadow, and one-audience downscope stages allow incremental rollout without changing request availability, but P6-F19 and schema compatibility are prerequisites.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise mixed policy generations and mixed binary versions through observe, enforce, epoch revocation, and rollback.

residualRisks: Forged or incomplete source events can bias risk analysis.
A compromised policy authority can still cause denial within its bounded scope.
Stale snapshots leave a bounded revocation window.
Semantic false positives can disrupt legitimate Agent collaboration.
Multiple action-owner integrations can drift without conformance tests.

affectedComponents: UniRouter identity, policy, gateway, streaming, and evidence components
X-Insight future ingestion, analysis, and risk-publication components
Tool, IAM, data, and export enforcement owners
workPackages: Define fact, risk-assertion, policy-snapshot, and enforcement-decision schemas with canonical signing vectors.
Build metadata-only fixtures and signed observe-mode conformance.
Add one bounded UniRouter model-route downscope audience.
Validate multi-instance outage, rotation, replay, rollback, and blast-radius behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: No risk assertion can increase authority or cross tenant/audience boundaries.
UniRouter continues local enforcement while X-Insight is unavailable.
Rollback is deterministic and does not rewrite evidence.
The first slice uses no raw content, paid request, external side effect, or target deployment.
Measured latency, memory, event lag, and revocation behavior meet explicitly accepted thresholds.
migrationNotes: Begin with metadata-only fixtures and one reversible model-route downscope.
Preserve last-known-good baseline policy and cross-generation compatibility.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop publishing the affected generation, advance its epoch if needed, and return the audience to the prior reviewed baseline without granting unlimited access.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the split plane under the current availability, ownership, and privacy constraints; begin only after the accepted identity, tenant, billing, capability, and stream prerequisites.

openQuestions: Which first model action may be automatically downscoped?
What assertion TTL, event-lag, revocation, clock-skew, and last-known-safe limits apply by action class?
Which broad downscopes require dual approval and rate containment?
Does the first version remain metadata-only?
Which component owns the future policy authority and signing keys?
What evidence proves complete mediation at future Tool, IAM, data, and export sinks?
